In this section, we provide an overview of a new approach to causal inference — *causal social-spatial network analysis*.  Whereas in causal social network analysis it is complicated to imagine the relationships between the sample and the universe (since the sample units are interrelated), in this approach we keep the simplicity of random sampling while engaging the insights possible to gain from networked analysis.



::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
# Learning goals

After this section, you will be equipped to:

- Write an NPSEM of the whole sample for a model that includes network generators  
- Draw the corresponding DANG  
- Apply the assumption of homogeneous network interference to an NPSEM that includes network generators  

:::
